summary: Training volume over the last 4 weeks has been very low, with only three recorded sessions — two indoor cardio efforts and one 5.2km open water swim — suggesting significant undertraining relative to the upcoming 5K open water race tomorrow (25 Oct) and the marathon 106 days away. Wellness data from late September shows consistently poor sleep (often under 4 hours) and very low body battery scores, indicating accumulated fatigue and recovery debt during that period. With the 5K swim race tomorrow and a marathon as the nearest A-race, the priority now is executing the race well, recovering properly post-race, and building a consistent training rhythm across all three disciplines.
suggestions: Prioritise sleep quality immediately — the data shows multiple nights under 3.5 hours which will severely limit adaptation; aim for 7–8 hours nightly starting tonight ahead of tomorrow's race.

Execute tomorrow's 5K open water race at a controlled, sustainable pace (similar to your recent 29:26/km open water effort) rather than going out too hard — treat it as a quality training stimulus, not an all-out effort given limited recent swim volume.
In Wk19 post-race, honour the easy recovery spin on Tuesday and resist adding extra volume — your body will need 48–72 hours to absorb the race stress before resuming structured training.

With the marathon 106 days out, begin integrating two quality run sessions per week from Wk19 onward, as running is currently absent from your recent 4-week log and needs to be re-established before long-run volume can safely build.

The Saturday long ride (60km, 240 min) on 24 Oct the day before race day is a significant fatigue risk — consider shortening it to a 30–45 minute easy spin to arrive at the swim race with fresher legs.

proposed_changes.reason: A full 4-hour long ride the day before a 5K open water race will leave legs and systemic fatigue elevated at race start; a short easy spin is the standard pre-race-eve protocol.
